author: NorthEast News Desk
body: India’s securities regulator has lifted most of a trading ban imposed on Copthall Mauritius Investment, a JPMorgan Chase unit, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.

The unit may return to regular trading, but it remains barred from participating in the market’s closing auction session while the regulator continues an investigation tied to an index-manipulation allegation. The partial restriction matters because closing auctions help establish widely referenced end-of-day prices.

The decision represents a change in the unit’s operating status rather than a conclusion to the underlying case. Reuters attributed the information to sources familiar with the matter, and the continued auction ban signals that regulatory review remains active.

For investors, the core development is access: Copthall can again participate in most market activity while facing a narrower limit at the close. The report does not establish wrongdoing, and an allegation is not a final regulatory finding. Any eventual order from the regulator could provide more detail about the conduct under review, the reason for easing the broader ban and whether further restrictions or penalties are possible.
dek: Copthall Mauritius may resume trading but remains excluded from closing auctions while an investigation continues.
headline: India lifts most of trading ban on JPMorgan unit, sources say
